answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor meets the 18% spend mandate, but switching the primary supplier while the line is at 94% of committed volume and has no buffer creates material delivery risk. Adding the low-cost vendor as a second source, while preserving incumbent continuity, is the best guarded path to capture savings and reduce single-source exposure. I am verifying memory_c3 because it is the most directly relevant evidence that dual sourcing protected allocation during a shortage.
